screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) Deep learning is the primary method (V-net-based CNN + 3D CRF-RNN); (2) Fully 3D/volumetric processing - all layers implemented in 3D, volumes resampled to 128x128x64; (3) Segments an anatomical organ (bladder); (4) CT modality; (5) Quantitative metrics reported (DSC 92.24%, VOE, RVD, ASD, MSD); (6) Novel contributions: first application of 3D fully connected CRF-RNN in medical image processing, novel dual-channel preprocessing, end-to-end joint training of CNN+CRF outperforming offline CRF post-processing. No exclusion criteria apply. Study type = 'method' (novel segmentation method; released code is an implementation of the method, not a general framework/toolkit, so not routed as 'framework').
title: Automatic bladder segmentation from CT images using deep CNN and 3D fully connected CRF-RNN
venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
architecture_details: V-net architecture (contracting/expansive paths with residual and skip connections) modified by adding batch normalization after each convolutional layer; 3D fully connected CRF-RNN (3D extension of Zheng et al.'s 2D CRF-RNN) plugged in after the CNN and trained end-to-end via mean-field inference as RNN; 3 mean-field iterations; kernel weights and label compatibility learned via backpropagation
preprocessing: Dual-channel preprocessing: density filter (wl=1030, ww=20) generates enhanced bladder density map stacked as second channel alongside original CT; resampling to 128x128x64 voxels at 2.0x2.0x3.0 mm3; data augmentation via random elastic deformations (50% probability) in slice plane
postprocessing: 3D fully connected CRF-RNN refinement integrated as part of the network (jointly trained, not offline post-processing); compared against and outperforms offline 3D CRF post-processing
datasets: ["Private clinical dataset (single hospital, multiple CT scanners)"]
dataset_size: 124 CT volumes (100 training / 24 validation); slices 256x256 or 512x512; 65-156 slices per volume
comparison_methods: ["V-net (reimplemented)", "V-net with dual-channel preprocessing", "V-net + batch normalization (their CNN)", "Dual-channel preprocessing + their CNN", "Their CNN + 3D CRF-RNN (ablation)", "Their CNN + 3D fully connected CRF as offline post-processing (ablation)"]
gpu_used: NVIDIA GTX 1080 Ti (11 GB); Intel Core i7-5960X CPU at 3.00 GHz
training_time: Not explicitly stated; two-stage training: 400 epochs CNN-only (lr=1e-4, batch=2) then 10 epochs fine-tuning with 3D CRF-RNN (lr=1e-7, batch=1); SGD, weight decay 0.0005, momentum 0.99
inference_time: 5.4 s per CT volume (vs. 0.9 s for V-net baseline)
limitations: False positive regions around bladder caused by soft-tissues/tumors with similar density that mislead the CRF long-range connections (and are amplified by dual-channel preprocessing); reported results may be over-fitted to validation set since no held-out test set was used; limited GPU memory restricts input size and batch size; average segmentation time (5.4 s) higher than baseline V-net (0.9 s)
future_work: Distinguish soft-tissues/tumors with appearance similar to bladder; collect more images and build a dedicated unseen test set; extend approach to other organs (liver, pancreas); investigate other modalities such as MRI

title: Prediction of major torso organs in low-contrast micro-CT images of mice using a two-stage deeply supervised fully convolutional network

Stage 1: global multi-organ network on whole torso; Stage 2: six organ-specific local networks on bounding-box crops from stage-1 predictions.

postprocessing: Threshold 0.01 on probability maps for binary labels; largest connected component extraction per organ for 3D bounding-box cropping (stage-2 input)
datasets: ["In-house mouse micro-CT dataset (Crump Institute, UCLA)"]
dataset_size: 40 contrast-enhanced micro-CT images (5-fold-style cross-validation: 35 train / 5 test, 8 repeats) + 10 real low-contrast micro-CT images (qualitative testing)
other_metrics: {"recovery_coefficient": "reported as box plots (TS-DSN closest to 1)", "precision": "reported as box plots (TS-DSN higher than FCN/DSN)", "recall": "reported as box plots (moderate; exact values not in text)", "dice_improvements_vs_SSM": "+18% left kidney, +26% spleen"}
comparison_methods: ["FCN (Shelhamer et al., no deep supervision)", "3D DSN (Dou et al., deep supervision without two-stage)", "SSM statistical shape model atlas registration (Wang et al. 2012b)", "Dense V-net (Gibson et al. 2018)"]

title: An Efficient and Accurate 3D Multiple-Contextual Semantic Segmentation Network for Medical Volumetric Images
venue: 2021 43rd Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine & Biology Society (EMBC)
architecture_details: Asymmetric unified 3D network. MCE extracts low/high-level contextual features (Fc1, Fc2), aligns resolutions via trilinear interpolation, fuses them by two concatenation-conv steps (Fs1 = conv([Fc1,Fc2]), Fs2 = conv([Fc1,Fs1])) with fixed 36 channels. Backbone is 3D residual blocks (3x3x3 kernels, Conv3D + InstanceNorm + ReLU) forming a light 3D ResU-Net with downsampling and concat-based upsampling path.
loss_function: Dice loss (with smoothness term sigma, minimized via derived gradient)
preprocessing: HU intensity truncation to [200, 250] HU as printed in paper (likely [-200, 250]); resampling to 2.0x2.0x2.0 mm3 (spleen) and 2.0x2.0x5.0 mm3 (liver); intensity normalization to [0, 1] for training/testing; random weight initialization
postprocessing: None — predictions made directly from single-model training/testing 'without relying on any post processing tools'

dataset_size: 181 CT scans total: 50 spleen (41 train / 9 test) + 131 liver (103 train / 28 test)
comparison_methods: ["3D U-Net", "V-Net", "VoxResNet", "3D DSD-FCN", "MultiResUNet"]

title: Precise Liver Tumor Segmentation in CT Using a Hybrid Deep Learning-Radiomics Framework
architecture: Cascaded 2.5D attention-dense U-Net (DenseNet-169 encoder) + radiomics RF false-positive suppression + compact 3D AlexNet-style boundary CNN
architecture_details: Two branches (liver; tumor conditioned on liver prob map as 4th input channel) sharing DenseNet-169 encoder (dense blocks 6/12/32/24, growth rate 32, compression 0.5, ~12M params/branch); UNet++-style nested dense skips; multi-scale attention gates (56/28/14/7); sub-pixel convolution decoder (r=2); input 3-slice axial stacks, 224x224 output. Stage 3: 728 radiomic features (histogram, gradient, RL, GLCM, shape, moments, boundary-band, 3D wavelet) reduced to 20 via intersection of 6 selection strategies (RFE, Lasso, RF/XGB/GBDT importance, Relief) -> random forest (350 trees, depth 16, 10 min samples/leaf). Stage 4: AlexNet-inspired 3D CNN, 11x11x11 patches, 3x3x3 convs (64/64/128/128/256) + FC, voxel relabeling in narrow band |signed distance|<=6.
loss_function: 0.7*Dice + 0.3*BCE; tumor task weight 2x liver; Adam lr 3e-4, batch 24, max 160 epochs, early stop patience 12
preprocessing: Resample to 1.0 mm in-plane (third-order B-spline), crop/pad to 224x224 around liver, HU clip [-100,400], linear rescale [0,255], 8-bit slice storage; 25 representative slices/volume for training; no data augmentation
postprocessing: Otsu adaptive thresholding per volume; 3x3 morphological closing; three-slice cranio-caudal consistency rule (restore if both neighbors foreground and avg prob >0.6, suppress isolated voxels); RF radiomics FP suppression; 3D CNN boundary refinement in narrow band |d|<=6
